content_html:
Visiting Machu Picchu is one of every traveler’s greatest dreams. However, the growth of tourism has created important challenges for its preservation.

The good news: it is possible to visit this wonder of the world responsibly, reducing your impact and contributing to its conservation.

Here’s how to do it.

Why Is Sustainable Tourism Important in Machu Picchu?

Every year, thousands of visitors travel from Cusco to Machu Picchu, generating:

  • Wear on trails and structures
  • Pollution
  • Pressure on the ecosystem
  • Impact on nearby communities

Practicing sustainable tourism helps protect this heritage site for future generations.

1. Choose Carefully How You Get There

Not all routes have the same impact.

More sustainable options:

  • Organized routes with controlled group sizes
  • Avoiding unregulated, improvised trips

Choosing the right route helps reduce pressure on the destination.

2. Respect the Rules Inside Machu Picchu

The site has clear conservation rules:

  • Stay on marked paths
  • Do not touch archaeological structures
  • Do not leave trash
  • Do not bring prohibited items

These rules are not optional—they are essential for preserving the site.

3. Reduce Your Environmental Impact

Simple actions make a difference:

  • Bring a reusable water bottle
  • Avoid single-use plastics
  • Take your waste with you
  • Use biodegradable sunscreen

Remember: what you bring in, you take out.

4. Support Local Communities

Tourism can be a positive force when done responsibly.

  • Hire local guides
  • Buy authentic handmade products
  • Spend money at local businesses

This helps your trip create real economic impact in the region.

5. Consider Less Crowded Alternatives

If you want a more authentic experience, explore nearby alternatives such as:

  • Sacred Valley
  • Choquequirao (less visited, more adventurous)

This helps reduce pressure on Machu Picchu.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many tourists affect the site without realizing it:

  • Leaving trash behind
  • Choosing informal operators
  • Ignoring schedules and route regulations

Avoiding these mistakes already makes you a more responsible traveler.

Is It Possible to Visit Machu Picchu Without Affecting the Environment?

The honest answer: zero impact does not exist—but you can minimize it as much as possible.

The key is:

Conscious decisions
Respect for regulations
Choosing responsible operators
Educating yourself as a traveler

Experience Machu Picchu Differently

A well-designed trip doesn’t just take you to a destination—it connects you with its history, people, and environment.
